proposals.evidence: CDIAL 135.1 aṅguli explicitly gives Maithili ā̃gur, Nepali aũlo and Lahnda aṅgal “finger”. The Maiya agui-type form is separately listed under 135.2 *aṅgūḍi and is assigned there; opaque reduced or retroflex-r forms remain distinct audit questions. Reviewed comparison: Dang ʌ̃ŋɡʌɾi “finger” (f_7ioamkt7uje7c). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8857 prastara explicitly gives Prakrit patthara and regional pathar/pathara “stone”, including known cross-IA loans. Unaspirated patar remains a qualified phonetic variant within this identifiable stone family. Reviewed comparison: Rana pʌtʰʌɾa “stone” (f_dgvm3jmtklaei). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

Survey maśīn and macharī match those documented paradigmatic/extended forms, not the separate matsiya branch. Reviewed comparison: Buksa mʌtʃʰi “fish” (f_niel6t4gubxrc). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 9349 bhaginī gives Bshk-area bai(n), Kashmiri biñ, Punjabi bhaiṇ and regional bahin/bheṇ “sister”. Simple n-retaining variants can be linked provisionally; additional r in baharṇ requires a separate morphological account. Reviewed comparison: NDu bahīnī “younger sister” (f_3ncbeg4zfyata). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10066 mārayati gives the mār- kill verb; maral/marla and māryo are ordinary eastern -l and western -y past/infinitive formations. Mār-diyo contains a give light verb and is not assigned as a simple inherited stem. Reviewed comparison: mewati_jhambaus mār “don't kill!, he killed” (f_p6alwpsz4guhw). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12598 śṛṇoti explicitly gives Bhojpuri sunal and western suṇṇo “hear”. Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology. Reviewed comparison: Buksa suna “he hears; he heard” (f_zzsmb6m2x457u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
